Use cases/AML & compliance

Automate KYC onboarding reviews from your written procedure

A KYC agent follows your onboarding procedure on each applicant: it reads the documents, runs the screening, applies your rules and asks a reviewer wherever the procedure says a person decides.

Book a demoSee how it runs

Works with

  • Custom REST

and any system with an API via Custom REST

What is a KYC onboarding review?

  • The procedure

    A KYC onboarding review checks that a new customer is who they say they are before the account opens. An analyst collects the ID and proof of address, screens the person and gives a risk rating under your policy. The judgment calls sit in the screening hits and the high-risk files.

  • What the agent does

    • Pulls the applicant, ID and proof of address from Sumsub

    • Checks each document against the sections of your procedure

    • Screens the applicant, directors and owners in ComplyAdvantage

    • Applies your risk rules and drafts any request for missing documents

  • What your team decides

    • Whether a possible PEP or sanctions match is the same person

    • Approval of any applicant rated High risk

    • Whether a request for documents goes to the applicant

    • Escalations to your MLRO or compliance officer

Setting up the KYC Review Agent

Connect your systems

Pull applicants and documents from Sumsub, screen in ComplyAdvantage, keep evidence in Google Drive, and reach any other system with an API through Custom REST.

  • Custom REST

Write the rules

Write the branch conditions once in CEL. Each run logs the rule that sent it to a reviewer or let it skip review.

Sample data
screening.hits > 0 || risk_rating == "High"Ask a reviewer
documents.missing.size() > 0Request documents
risk_rating != "High"Approve

Add reviewers where the procedure says

The agent stops where your procedure says a person decides, shows the evidence it gathered, and resumes on the reviewer's decision.

Start it from the event

Start a review when Sumsub marks an applicant as reviewed, or when your onboarding system posts a new applicant to a webhook. A daily schedule picks up applicants still waiting on documents.

  • Sumsub · applicantReviewed
  • Daily at 06:00 · applicants awaiting documents
  • Inbound webhook · new applicant

Version and evaluate

Write test scenarios for a clean applicant, a screening hit and a missing document. Each new version of the KYC review runs them first, and a failing scenario blocks publishing.

Questions about KYC onboarding automation

Does the agent approve applicants on its own?

Only where your procedure allows it. In the clean example the rating is Medium and no rule calls for a person, so the agent approves and logs the rule it used. A screening hit or a High rating pauses the run.

Which systems does it read from?

Sumsub for the applicant and documents, ComplyAdvantage for screening and Google Drive for the case folder. Other systems with an API connect through Custom REST.

What happens when a document is missing?

The agent drafts the request and a reviewer approves it. Your team sends it, and the run waits until the document arrives.

Can we change the risk rules later?

Yes. Edit the procedure or its CEL rules and publish a new version. Finished runs keep the version they followed, and new runs use the new one.

Controls your auditors will ask about

These controls apply to each agent you build. Sample data

    • Admin
    • Author
    • Reviewer
    • Auditor

    Role-based access

    Admin, Author, Reviewer and Auditor roles, scoped to each workspace.

    • 417c2e…
    • 42a91f… ← 7c2e
    • 4303d8… ← a91f

    Hash-chained audit log

    Each entry carries the hash of the one before it. Verifying the log recomputes the chain and flags entries that no longer match.

  • v1.1v1.2v1.3Published

    Versioned specs

    Each run records the exact version it followed; old versions stay readable.

  • * * * * * * * *vault/sumsub/key

    Secrets in a vault

    Steps point to a vault path, and the key stays in the vault.

    • Signed delivery✓ accepted
    • Unsigned delivery✕ rejected

    Signed webhook triggers

    Unsigned or stale deliveries are rejected before a run starts.

  • SandboxLive

    Sandbox before live

    New versions run on test data first. Going live is a separate step.
